Author: Samit Gopal
Bench: Samit Gopal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:194875 Court

10057 of 2024 Applicant :- Yash Yadav Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Applicant :-
Sarvesh Kumar Dubey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Samit Gopal,

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
J. 1. Heard Sri
Sarvesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri V.D. Ojha, learned counsel for the State
and perused the record.

2.  The present anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant-Yash Yadav is titled as Criminal Misc. IInd Anticipatory Bail Applicaion with the following prayers:- "It is therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to allow this application and release the applicant on anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest in connection with Case Crime No.545 of 2018, u/s 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Mainpuri in pursuance of FIR dated 16.5.2018 during the pendency of trial, on such terms and condition as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper, otherwise the applicant shall suffer irreparable loss and injury.

It is further prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to release the applicant on interim bail in event of his arrest in connection with Case Crime No.545 of 2018, u/s 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Mainpuri during the pending hearing and final disposal of this application on terms and conditions as this Hon'ble Court deem fit and proper otherwise the applicant shall suffer irreparable loss and injury."

3. Previously the applicant and co-accused Roman Sardar @ Ishdeep Singh filed an anticipatory bail application before this Court being Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.18154 of 2021 (Yash Yadav and another Vs. State of U.P. and another) which was decided vide order dated 7.12.2021 passed by another Bench of this Court directing that the applicants therein shall be released on anticipatory bail till submission of police report, if any, under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. before the competent court subject to the conditions in the said order

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.18154 of 2021 (Yash Yadav and another Vs. State of U.P. and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the said order reads as under:- "Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Abhinav Prasad (Brief Holder) learned counsel appearing for the State and perused the record.
It is contended on behalf of the applicant that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
They did not commit any offence as alleged.
It is further submitted that they have been implicated in the present due to ulterior motive.
The applicants have no criminal antecedent.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, considering the nature of accusation and the fact that they have no criminal antecedent, the applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case.
In the event of arrest of the applicants (i). Yash Yadav (ii).

Roman Sardar @ Ishdeep Singh involved in Case Crime No.545 of 2018, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District Mainpuri, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report,
if any, under section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. before the competent Court on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:- (i) the applicants shall make themselves available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required; (ii) the applicants Yash Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158604905/
1 shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office; (iii) the applicants shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if they have passport the same shall be deposited by them before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicants.

The Investigating Officer is directed to conclude the investigation of the present case in accordance with law expeditiously preferably within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order independently without being prejudice by any observation made by this Court while considering and deciding the present anticipatory bail application of the applicants.
The applicants are directed to produce a certified of this order, before the S.S.P./S.P. concerned within ten days from today, who shall ensure the compliance of present order."
4. Subsequently there appears to be a Criminal Misc. Second Modification Application filed in the same which was rejected vide order dated 2.4.2024 passed by another Bench of this court.
The said order reads as under:- "Order on Criminal Misc. (IInd Modification) Application No.3 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. (IInd Modification) Application No.3 of 2024
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant.
The present second modification application is misconceived and is accordingly, rejected" 5.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the applicant was initially granted anticipatory bail in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.18154 of 2021 till submission of police report, if any, under Section 173(2)
Cr.P.C. vide order dated 7.12.2021 subsequent to which a modification application was filed for modifying the said order since at a belated stage it came to the knowledge of the applicant that on account of typographical error in the order dated 7.12.2021, the said anticipatory bail application was allowed till submission of charge sheet only.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.18154 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is next submitted that the said modification application was rejected vide order dated 2.4.2024 on the ground of delay and laches, para 21 and 22 of the affidavit in support of present anticipatory bail application have been placed before this Court, the same read as under:- "21.

That at a very belated stage, it came to the knowledge of the applicant that on account of typographical error in the order dated 07.12.2021, the said anticipatory bail application was allowed till the submission of the charge sheet, whereas it ought to have been till the submission of the trial.

22. That faced with the abovementioned situation, the applicants approached this Hon'ble Court by filing correction/modification application before this Hon'ble Court on 26.07.2023, which was not traceable, hence a subsequent application was filed on 28.03.2024 and this Hon'ble Court vide its order dated 02.04.2024 had rejected the said application merely on the ground of delay and latches.
A copy of the order dated 02.04.2024 passed by this Hon'ble Court is being filed herewith and marked as Annexure No.9 to this affidavit."

6. It is submitted that in the meantime co-accused Ashish Yadav was granted anticipatory bail vide order dated 1.4.2022 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.20414 of 2021 (Ashish Yadav Vs. State of U.P. and another) till conclusion of trial, copy of the said order has been placed before the Court which is Annexure No.10.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant and another co-accused preferred a Criminal Misc. Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. No.13095 of 2024 (Yash Yadav and another Vs. State) which was dismissed by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 20.8.2024 on the ground of delay and laches.

It is submitted that the applicant has been pursuing the remedies available to him under law and since his previous anticipatory bail application prayer was only granted till filing of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. and the investigation concluded and a charge sheet dated 31.8.2019 was submitted against the applicant Yash Yadav, co-accused Ashish Yash Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158604905/
2 Yadav and Roman Sardar @ Ishdeep Singh on which the court concerned took cognizance vide order dated 19.12.2020 and summoned the said accused persons, the case of the applicant is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.

entities.text: Ashish Yash Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer made in the anticipatory bail application and submitted that the facts of the matter go to show that the applicant was granted stay of arrest till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. vide order dated 30.5.2018 passed by a Division Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.14219 of 2018 (Yash Yadav and two others Vs. Sate of U.P. and others).

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.14219 of 2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yash Yadav and two others Vs. Sate of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that charge sheet in the matter has been submitted on which cognizance has been taken vide order dated 19.12.2020.

It is further submitted that subsequent to taking of cognizance by the court concerned, the applicant has been avoiding the process of law despite the fact that he knows that charge sheet has been filed and cognizance has been taken against him and he has been summoned as a result of which the trial court is issuing bailable warrant against him repeatedly since the last about four years.

It is submitted that even the challenge to the charge sheet dated 30.9.2019, the order taking cognizance/summoning order dated 19.12.2020 and the entire proceedings of the said case before the Court was dismissed in Application U/S 482 No.13095 of 2024 vide order dated 20.8.2024, the said order has been placed before the Court which is annexure no.11 to the affidavit which reads as under:- "Heard Miss Roshani Dwivedi, the learned counsel for applicants and the learned A.G.A. for State. Perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr. P. C. has been filed challenging the charge sheet dated 30.9.2019 submitted in Case Crime No.
545 of 2018, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 IPC, P.S. Kotwali, District Mainpuri, the Cognizance Taking Order/Summoning Order dated 19.12.2020 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Mainpuri in Criminal Case No. 2875 of 2020 (State Vs. Yash Yadav and others) under Sections 420,
476, 468, 471, 406 IPC, P.S. Kotwali, District Mainpuri as well as the entire proceedings of aforementioned Criminal case now pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mainpuri.

entities.text: State Vs. Yash Yadav and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mainpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. has raised a preliminary objection by submitting that present application has been filed after expiry of a period of 4 years and 6 months from the date of charge sheet and after expiry of a period of 3 years and 3 months from the date of the Cognizance Taking Order/Summoning Order.
As such, present application is hopelessly barred by laches.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant invited attention of Court to the averment made in paragraph 21 of the affidavit filed in support of present application.

For ready reference, the same is reproduced herein under:- "That faced with the abovementioned situation, the applicants approached this Hon'ble Court by filing correction/modification application before this Hon'ble Court on 26.07.2023, which was not traceable, hence a subsequent application was filed on 28.03.2024 and this Hon'ble Court vide its order dated 02.04.2024 had rejected the said application merely on the ground of delay and latches.
A copy of the order dated 02.04.2024 passed by this Hon'ble Court is being filed herewith and marked as Annexure No. 9 to this affidavit."
The explanation offered in paragraph 21 of the affidavit filed in support of present application, does not appear to be sufficient in the opinion of the Court.
As such, the laches in filing present application have not been sufficiently explained.
In view of above, present application fails and is liable to be dismissed.
It is, accordingly, dismissed."

8. It is further submitted that looking to the fact that the applicant has been avoiding the process of law since last about four years and has been absconding,
this Court should not entertain the present anticipatory bail application in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of State of Haryana vs. Dharamraj, 2023 SCC Online SC 1085 and Srikant Upadhyay and others Vs. State of Bihar and another : SLP (Criminal) No. 7940 of 2023 Yash Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158604905/
3 decided on 14.03.2024, and thus the present anticipatory bail application be rejected.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yash Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. After having heard learned counsel for the parties, it is evident that the applicant subsequent to filing of charge sheet, cognizance and summoning vide order dated 19.12.2020 has been avoiding the process of law and has not appeared before the trial court concerned.
It is about four years since then.
Even challenge to the criminal proceedings, charge sheet and summoning order has been dismissed by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 20.8.2024 on the ground of laches.
10. The present anticipatory bail application is thus rejected.
(Samit Gopal, J.)
